synopsis: Over a summer evening in the cafe, Alex hands the class the term's biggest news in its flattest voice — a job in Japan, next month, already decided — and the room refuses to let the send-off slide past while refusing just as hard to crown his leaving as brave. As Aakash sets his own uncertain camera road-trip beside the move and Mira returns to the group chat with no apology, the class states each future in its honest modality and holds leaving, staying, and undecided level, none ranked above the others.

forbiddenClaims: surname, guessed kana name, nationality, or private history beyond warm owner-authorised texture
departure framed as the brave or correct future, or ranked above staying or undecided
voice opened into eloquent vulnerability under pressure rather than narrowing further
surname, guessed kana name, nationality, or private history
energetic invitation overriding a stated no
leaving framed as braver than staying or than his own open plan
surname, guessed kana name, nationality, address, or private history
return framed as needing a guilt explanation or an invented cause of absence

scenes.goal: Meet Alex delivering the biggest news of the term in the flattest register in the room, and let the class refuse to let the send-off slide past without turning his leaving into a brave act.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: When the biggest fact lands in the calmest clause, will the room catch it and mark it on his terms?
scenes.learnerNeed: A stance on how to meet a flat, enormous announcement — naming the load-bearing clause the calm was hiding, and keeping the send-off from inflating.

nodes.description: Before Alex has finished taking off his jacket, Aakash's phone already shows a draft poll titled ALEX SEND-OFF: dinner, camera walk, or a full Saturday route. Alex reads all three options, sets his own phone beside it, and says the part Aakash has got ahead of.

nodes.intent: Deliver the term's biggest news in the flattest possible register, letting the load-bearing clause — next month, and already decided — land the calmest of all.
nodes.attentionTarget: the gap in the conversation, and how little he raises his voice to fill it

nodes.intent: Refuse to let the biggest clause pass flat — catch what he under-stressed, name it back, and ask, leaving him room to decline, to mark the leaving properly.
nodes.attentionTarget: the buried clause 'next month, already settled' and Alex's refusal to raise it

nodes.intent: Under attention his voice narrows rather than opens — accept a send-off only if it stays small, and name the real uncertainty plainly without dramatizing it.
nodes.attentionTarget: how little he wants made of it, and the parts he genuinely has not decided

nodes.question: Alex has handed you the biggest news of the term in the flattest voice in the room. How do you meet it?

options.action: Say the load-bearing clause back to him, plainly, so the calm doesn't hide it.

nodes.resume: The learner has met the flat announcement — either naming the clause Alex under-stressed, or holding the send-off to his size. Alex answers by setting the terms he can live with.

nodes.intent: Accept a small send-off on plain terms, and refuse in advance to be made the one who did the brave thing.
nodes.attentionTarget: the difference between being seen off and being held up as an example

nodes.description: Aakash deletes the three-option draft and sends a two-choice poll: usual cafe, or no separate event. Phones light around the table. Alex votes for the cafe, then turns his screen face-down before anyone can add a speech field.

scenes.goal: Let the class lay its different futures — leaving, staying, undecided — side by side, and hold them without ranking any above the others.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: When one person's 'someday in Japan' finally comes true, does the room rank it above the ones still open?
scenes.learnerNeed: A transfer where the learner states each person's future in honest modality and refuses the comparative frame that would crown one.

nodes.description: The group chat fills with half-plans: one person's 'someday, for work,' another's 'maybe never,' a third's 'not decided.' After a long quiet in the thread, a familiar name surfaces at the bottom, typing from somewhere hours behind them.

nodes.intent: Put his own future on the table as a genuine maybe — the solo camera road-trip — and hold it beside Alex's decided move without ranking either.
nodes.attentionTarget: his road-trip as a hope he hasn't committed to, not a lesser version of Alex's move

nodes.intent: Return after a long absence without a shred of apology, pick the thread straight up, refuse to let the futures be ranked, and invite a lapsed learner to restart with no pressure.
nodes.attentionTarget: the three kinds of 'someday' in the thread, held level, and an open hand to whoever stalled

nodes.resume: Three kinds of future sit in the thread — decided, undecided, staying. The learner takes them up and states each in its honest form, without lifting one over the others.

nodes.resumeContext: The learner phrases each person's future in the modality it actually has — Alex's move as decided (〜ことになった / もう決まった), Aakash's trip as a genuine maybe (〜かもしれない / 〜たいと思っている / まだわからない), someone's staying as its own settled choice — and joins them without a comparative word that would rank one above another.

nodes.description: The three futures are set out as three cards at the same height — leaving, staying, undecided. Only the card that got ranked, or forced into a certainty it did not have, comes back to be restated; the ones already phrased honestly stay put.

nodes.resume: The three futures now sit level, each in its own honest modality. Alex looks at them lined up and says what his leaving is, and is not.

nodes.intent: Land the term's drifting 'someday, for work' on himself as payoff, and refuse the frame that would make his decided departure braver than a staying or an undecided one.
nodes.attentionTarget: the group's old 'someday, for work' phrase, now his, and the three futures held level

nodes.description: Alex's cafe vote remains the only mark on the send-off poll. Mira's twenty-minute review invitation sits below it with no reply required. Aakash closes the route-planning tab without booking anything, and the cafe receipt pins the phones in place when the door opens.

callbacks.meaningNow: Alex delivers the term's biggest event — an actual move to Japan — in the flattest possible register, and the class has finally learned to listen for the unstressed clause ('next month, already settled'); his understatement is now something the room can decode and mark, not miss, and it is used to keep the departure ordinary rather than heroic.
callbacks.optionalFallback: Alex announces a large, decided plan very plainly and the class marks it without inflating it, whether or not the learner recalls his earlier flat-delivery beats.

outcomes.description: Alex's decided move to Japan is announced in the flattest register and marked with a small send-off on his terms; the class lays its leaving, staying, and undecided futures side by side and holds them level, ranking none as the brave one.

Alex delivers his actual move to Japan in the flattest possible register and names his own uncertainty plainly rather than opening into a speech; he accepts a small send-off on his terms and refuses to be crowned the brave one, leaving departure ordinary and his return date genuinely open.

Aakash puts his solo camera road-trip on the table as a real maybe and, for once, does not accelerate it or the send-off into an event; the reflex-organizer sits with an open plan and lets it stay undecided beside Alex's settled one.

Mira returns to the group chat after a long absence with no apology theatre, picks the thread straight up, holds the class's different futures level, and invites a lapsed learner to restart with an explicit easy-out; the group treats her restart as normal rather than a debt.
Plans-under-uncertainty and non-comparative-futures evidence returns through the chapter's transfer activity; the story emits no lesson-completion command, and no registered N1 package is claimed.

replay.withdrawnContentFallback: Use the same flat-announcement and non-comparative-futures beats with neutral nameplates: a classmate announces a decided move very plainly, a friend keeps an open trip undecided beside it, a distant member returns without guilt, and the class states each future in its honest modality without ranking one as braver.
